Tacit

/TAS-it/ - the stress falls on TAS · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tacit means understood or expressed without words.

There is a tacit seating chart in the faculty lounge, and the new hire learned it by taking Hal's chair exactly once.

Worked Example

Nobody at the firehouse ever voted on it, and no plaque announces it, but a tacit rule governs the last pancake at Sunday breakfast: it waits for whoever took the worst call that week. Rookies absorb the habit in a month of watching, and the rule has never once needed words.

Tacit is the precise adjective because it means understood or expressed without words — the rule is fully in force and completely unspoken, which is the whole trick of it. Unspoken is the plain twin; tacit adds the sense of shared understanding, and its opposite is this unit's explicit, where everything is spelled out.

How Tacit Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unspoken

unspoken: the plain-English twin — simply never said aloud

understood

understood: settled between people, perhaps after words long ago

Antonyms

explicit

explicit: spelled out in so many words — this unit's own opposite

stated

stated: put into words, on the record

How Strong Is It? — implied → tacit → unthinking

implied vs. tacit

implied vs. tacit: Implied stops short of tacit — an implied warning still rides on words somebody actually said; a tacit rule was never spoken at all.

unthinking vs. tacit

unthinking vs. tacit: Unthinking goes further than tacit — a tacit pact is understood by everyone it binds, while an unthinking habit runs before understanding even wakes.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tacit

Root — tacit: silent, unspoken (Latin tacitus, from tacere, 'to be silent')

Put it together

Put it together: Tacit IS its root: Latin tacitus, 'passed over in silence,' from tacere, 'to be silent.' Nothing peels off — English borrowed the hush whole. Every tacit agreement keeps the Roman sense working: binding, real, and never once said.

Where the silent root turns up next

Where the silent root turns up next: Latin tacere kept working after tacit: it built taciturn, for a person so sparing with words they seem sealed shut — a word waiting for you later in this course. Musicians meet the root cold, too: a part marked tacet sits out the whole movement in silence.

Word Building

Word Choice

formal / precise

Tacit is for things in force without ever being said: approval, truces, rules. Its exact opposite is this unit's explicit. Unspoken overlaps, but tacit stresses that everyone involved understands and abides — silence with a handshake inside it.
